answer: English proficiency is required for admission to any CAS program; students who do not meet the University's English requirement may gain admission through the Intensive English Program.

answer: Incoming Computer Science, Healthcare Information Systems and Mathematics students must pass the mathematics placement exam; those with a low score must take one or two remedial courses (MATH 190 Calculus I, MATH 191 Calculus II) before program-level calculus.

answer: The remedial courses MATH 190 and MATH 191 do not count toward fulfilling CAS degree requirements.

answer: All CAS students take nine credits of mandatory foundational courses: ARAB 212 Arabic Language and Communication (2), a Community & Sustainability course (1), ENGL 210 English Composition and Rhetoric (3), and ENGL 217 Professional English Communication (3).

answer: CAS program requirements are program-specific and split into major and non-major categories, each with mandatory and elective courses; details are in each student's Student Study Plan (SSP).

source_quote: The first digit in the three-digit course number indicates the course level: 1 for freshman,
answer: CAS course codes are a four-letter prefix plus a three-digit number; the first digit is the level: 1 freshman, 2 sophomore, 3 junior, 4 senior, 5 graduate (e.g., EDUC 201 is a sophomore-level education course).

CAS course prefixes include ADPR Advertising and Public Relations, ARAB Arabic, CMNS Communications, COSC Computer Science, EDUC Education, ENGL English, GRDS Graphic Design, HCIS Healthcare Information Systems, HIST History, IELP Intensive English, INDS Interior Design, JRSM Journalism, MATH Mathematics, POSC Political Science, PSYC Psychology, SOCI Sociology.
Credit notation c(t,p): c = total credit hours, t = theoretical (lecture) hours, p = practical/lab hours. For example, 3(3,0) is a 3-credit course with 3 lecture hours and 0 lab hours.

answer: The CAS Learning Support Center (LSC), in Block I and open to all students throughout the week, offers peer-to-peer tutoring by upper-level Teaching Assistants with on-call faculty, and resources such as books, study guides, course materials and internet-connected PCs.
